mechanism_narrative: A sustained federal funds rate below 0.2% compresses discount rates for equity cash flows, generating positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days as accommodative policy supports valuation expansion.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS < 0.2%.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate exceeds 9.5%, it signals economic contraction that reduces corporate earnings growth expectations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 40% of instances when UNRATE > 9.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) above their 12-month moving averages indicates robust consumer demand, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days through earnings momentum.
failure_condition: The joint signal (HOUST and RSAFS both > 12-mo avg) is associated with negative 20-day returns in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: In a monetary tightening cycle (FEDFUNDS > 0.5% and CPIAUCSL > 215), rate hikes reduce future cash flow growth expectations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 0.5% and CPIAUCSL > 215.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained industrial production index (INDPRO) above 95 indicates expanding manufacturing output, supporting corporate earnings growth and generating positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: INDPRO > 95 is associated with negative 20-day returns in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) fall below 550, it signals deep housing market contraction that triggers government stimulus and equity market recovery, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances when HOUST < 550.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle labor market expansion (PAYEMS growth > 0.5% monthly and UNRATE < 5.0%), strong job growth supports consumer spending and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of instances when PAYEMS growth > 0.5% and UNRATE < 5.0%.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 0.2% and consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) above 215 indicates an inflationary monetary tightening cycle, reducing equity valuations and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint signal (FEDFUNDS > 0.2% and CPIAUCSL > 215) is associated with positive 60-day returns in more than 40% of cases.
